items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: I heard him play. He played it better than anybody that I'd ever heard play before. I says, all right, you want the job?

ctx.x: Did your piano play just the straight chords?

Play chords and he played bass, played bass and contramelody. We were able to fill in. In other words, he'd have to know the rhythm twice, play the chords, and he played bass too. You see, there was bass hand. And the other one he played, contramelodies, no melody. All contramelodies and harmonies. And that's what he was to play. And I couldn't get to these fellows. All they played bird music up on top of the piano. Bird music. There was no foundation tone and they disrupt the band. Now, along comes Robinson. He…
I'm sorry, I didn't get anything about the trombone player.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Robertson joined us as piano player which he had been the first steady piano player after Regis' death.

ctx.x: I hate to interrupt you on that story but I missed out a couple of things. I didn't get who was in the band at the time. I know Edwards was back. He replaced Christian and I didn't get the names of the other bands.

Now I'll tell you the names of the men. Robertson joined us as piano player which he had been the first steady piano player after Regis' death. We had Shields, myself, Spobara, Edwards and what's his name? Roberts had made the five of us.
And that's immediately upon coming back from London. That's right. Robertson Hilton. And then what was the name of the saxophone players? I want to get that to you.

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-16
items.q: He just ignored me, just kept on playing his piano. The next day I gave him his two weeks' notice, and I replaced him.

ctx.x: Well, we forgot about Lytel and Frankie Signorelli. About 1920, Signorelli joined my band. At that time they may have had a Memphis Five, but I never heard of them stopping the machine. Well, I had a little bit of friction with Roberson. He had promised the band a thousand dollars if I put Margie over. Well, I saw the plug of Margie for him, sang it for him, placed it on the record for him, and after he got his first statement, he didn't say anything. I asked him about what he was going to do to three of them.…

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: Out of the whole original jazz band that you had in Chicago and later in New York, the only one who could actually read music was the piano player, Russell Robinson.

ctx.x: I had to have something new tunes. So I'd take some of these old tunes like Shine on Harvest Moon. Take the chord construction. I made the jazz band ball out of it. I'd take old pieces like the Georgia Camp Meeting Ball. I made the fidgeted feet out of it. The last part I put on myself. But the rest of it are the same chord constructions. But you know, I played a little chords on the piano. And I understood it. Most old fakers you will find can play three or four instruments.

Yes, that we know. Now, Nick, let me clarify this. Because remember, you and I are talking as musicians. But the people who are listening to us don't know exactly what we mean. Out of the whole original jazz band that you had in Chicago and later in New York, the only one who could actually read music was the piano player, Russell Robinson.
Well, that came in later years after Ragus had died.
